chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn Saʿīd, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Ziyād, from Jaʿfar, from his forefathers, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said:
The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “Excellent is the shroud: the robe; and excellent is the sacrificial offering: the horned ram.”
Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: This report agrees with the ʿāmmah, and we do not act upon it, because we have explained that it is not permissible for the shroud to be of silk.

key_terms.الْأُضْحِيَّةُ: the sacrificial offering made on the occasion of sacrifice
key_terms.الْإِبْرِيسَمِ: silk, stated here as impermissible material for a shroud
key_terms.الْحُلَّةُ: a robe or garment mentioned here as a type of shroud
key_terms.الْخَبَرُ: the transmitted report or hadith under discussion
key_terms.الْعَامَّةَ: the Sunni majority, whose view this report is said to accord with
key_terms.الْكَبْشُ الْأَقْرَنُ: a horned ram, described here as an excellent sacrificial animal
key_terms.الْكَفَنُ: the burial shroud used for the deceased

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a kafan to be made of silk according to this hadith in Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a statement attributed to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم regarding the shroud and the sacrificial animal. Shaykh al-Ṭūsī then notes that the report accords with the view of the ʿāmmah and is not acted upon, since a shroud made of silk is not considered permissible. The passage is therefore significant in the context of legal evaluation of hadith and rulings concerning burial.
